collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and another adult; in the story (name1) has a long-term illness that tires (him/her) easily)

collection.description: A villager with a tiring illness rests halfway up the hill, and a passer-by calls them lucky: explain why, or let it go.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Halfway up the hill to the gardens there's a flat stone, and (subject) always stops there to rest. (subject.He/she) has an illness that wears out (subject.his/her) strength quickly, and the hill is long. Today, as (subject.he/she) sits, (friend) passes on the way up and calls out, half joking, "Resting already? Lucky you!"

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "It's not lucky," (subject) says evenly. "My body gets tired faster than yours. If I rest here, I can work all morning up there. If I don't, I'm finished by the top." (friend) stops. (friend.He/she) hadn't known. "I'm sorry," (friend.he/she) says. "I thought you just liked the view." "I do like the view," says (subject). "That's a bonus."

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) waves and doesn't bother explaining. (subject.He/she) has explained a lot of times, to a lot of people. Later, in the gardens, (subject) out-plants (friend) all morning, steadily and without fuss. (friend) notices. On the way back down (friend) sits on the resting stone for a moment too. (friend.He/she) doesn't say anything. Neither does (subject).
